head: The weakest console
won the war.
slides.sub: How Nintendo stopped chasing gamers and found everyone else.

image.label: A family laughing in a living room, swinging controllers
image.brief: 거실에서 온 가족이 리모컨형 컨트롤러를 휘두르며 웃는 장면. 실제 제품 디자인과 로고는 쓰지 않음.

head: The race was
about power.
body: In the mid-2000s, Sony and Microsoft were building ever more powerful consoles, with sharper graphics and higher prices.
Nintendo's previous console, the GameCube, had fallen behind both.

image.label: Two huge glowing consoles facing off
image.brief: 거대한 게임기 두 대가 빛을 내며 맞서는 구도. 브랜드 없음.

head: Games got
harder to start.
body: Controllers had more buttons. Games took hours to learn. People who did not already play felt shut out, and many former players had drifted away.

image.label: A controller covered in buttons
image.brief: 버튼이 잔뜩 달린 복잡한 컨트롤러 클로즈업.

head: You are behind on power.
What do you build next?
body: Two richer rivals are racing on graphics. You can't win that race on spending.

options.text: The most powerful console yet, to catch up
options.feedback: You would be fighting two richer rivals on their terms. Keep swiping.

options.text: Something cheaper and simpler, for people who don't play
options.feedback: This is the bet Nintendo made. Keep swiping.

options.text: Leave hardware and make games for rival consoles
options.feedback: Safer, but it gives up your own platform. Keep swiping.

image.label: A crossroads sign in a game world

head: A remote you
just swing.
body: The Wii launched in late 2006 with a motion controller shaped like a TV remote. You swung it like a racket or a bowling ball.
In many markets Wii Sports came in the box, so anyone could start in seconds.

image.label: A hand swinging a remote like a tennis racket
image.brief: 테니스 라켓처럼 리모컨을 휘두르는 손, 동작선 그래픽.

slides.label: US launch price, about half that of the cheaper PlayStation 3
body: Simpler parts kept the price low and let Nintendo earn money on each console from the start.

image.label: A price tag next to a white console

head: Grandparents
started bowling.
body: Families played together. News reports described retirement homes running Wii bowling leagues.
For a long time, stores struggled to keep it in stock.

image.label: Seniors bowling in a community room
image.brief: 양로원 거실에서 노인들이 게임으로 볼링을 치는 장면. 실루엣 위주.

slides.label: Wii consoles sold, according to Nintendo
body: It outsold both of its more powerful rivals in that generation.

image.label: Stacks of white console boxes
image.brief: 천장까지 쌓인 흰 게임기 상자. 로고 없음.

head: Stop fighting rivals.
Find new players.
body: Instead of competing on what rivals measured, power and graphics, Nintendo picked a different customer: people who did not play games.
It gave up what they did not care about and doubled down on what they did: simple, social fun at a low price.

image.label: Many people around one screen
image.brief: 화면 하나를 둘러싼 다양한 나이의 사람들.

head: Who isn't buying
from anyone yet?
body: Sometimes the biggest market is the people nobody is serving.
**Try it today:** name a group that avoids your whole category. What makes it too hard or too expensive for them?

image.label: An empty sofa waiting for players
image.brief: 플레이어를 기다리는 빈 소파와 켜진 TV.

factChecks.note: Wii 북미 출시일(2006년 11월 19일)과 미국 출시 가격 $249.99, PS3 출시 가격($499/$599)은 Nintendo·Sony 발표로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2006년 11월 19일 북미 출시, 약 250달러, PS3 499·599달러 확인.
Wii Sports 동봉은 북미·유럽 등 기준이고 일본에서는 별매였습니다. 카드에는 "in many markets"로 적었습니다.
Wii 누적 판매 1억 163만 대는 Nintendo 공식 자료 기준입니다. 같은 세대 PS3(약 8,700만), Xbox 360(약 8,400만)은 추정치가 자료마다 달라 카드에 숫자를 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 누적 1억 163만 대는 이번 검색에서 미확인.
비게이머를 겨냥한 전략은 Nintendo 투자자 설명회와 이와타 사토루 사장의 발언(게임 인구 확대)에 근거합니다. 직접 인용은 넣지 않았습니다.
양로원 Wii 볼링 리그는 2007년 무렵 미국 언론 보도 기준입니다.
